availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: Show available commands

availableCommands.name: a11y-audit
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to check a frontend for accessibility. Covers keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, color contrast, focus management, and WCAG alignment.

availableCommands.name: afk-loop
availableCommands.description: Use when you want the agent to work unattended through local Markdown implementation issues, picking the next ready task from a DAG of blocking relationships.

availableCommands.name: agent-cost-guard
availableCommands.description: Use when monitoring token cost per loop, detecting token maxing, or limiting parallel subagents to control cost and context pressure.

availableCommands.name: agent-reach
availableCommands.description: Use when researching trends or public sources across credential-free channels (YouTube transcripts/metadata, RSS/Atom feeds). Routes to extensions/agent-reach/wrapper.py, a whitelist passthrough to the agent-reach CLI (`get` grammar)

availableCommands.name: agentic-rag
availableCommands.description: Use when implementing an agentic RAG product in a target project (support desk, knowledge assistant, evidence-gated Q&A). Playbook for the retrieve -> decision-gate -> answer-or-escalate architecture with multimodal index and human-review loop. Builds the system; does not answer questions with it.

availableCommands.name: ai-coding-dictionary
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks about AI coding jargon, wants to clarify a term like context engineering, harness engineering, prompt engineering, or agent harness, or when the agent needs to agree on a term definition before continuing a technical discussion.

availableCommands.name: ai-tools
availableCommands.description: Use when running local, offline-first ML tooling (mechanistic interpretability PoCs like refusal-direction ablation on local safetensors or the HF cache), when adding self-contained model experiments that print JSON, or when post-training, distilling (s1K/R1-style), or RLVR/GRPO-tuning a reasoning or domain model.

availableCommands.name: ai3d-gen
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for generative 3D assets (text-to-3D, image-to-3D, mesh synthesis) via self-hosted open models. Routes to extensions/comfyui-operator/wrapper.py against a local ComfyUI server, with direct-model fallbacks (TRELLIS, TripoSG, InstantMesh, Hunyuan3D). All free/open weights, no paid SaaS.

availableCommands.name: animation-direction
availableCommands.description: Use when turning narrated video/audio into synced code-rendered motion graphics — narration -> timestamped transcript -> scene plan -> approval gate -> Remotion render -> ffmpeg composite. Covers the motion vocabulary, beat-to-visual mapping, scene-plan v2 schema, and the mandatory plan gate via extensions/asr + extensions/remotion-render.

availableCommands.name: api-context-spec
availableCommands.description: Use when generating or maintaining OpenAPI specs as context for AI agents. Ensures API contracts are explicit, versioned, and machine-readable.

availableCommands.name: api-design
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to design, review, or document an API. Covers REST, OpenAPI, versioning, error models, contract testing, and authentication.

availableCommands.name: api-spec
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to design, review, or document an API (REST, OpenAPI, versioning, error models, contract testing, authentication), or when generating/maintaining OpenAPI specs as machine-readable context for AI agents.

availableCommands.name: architecture
availableCommands.description: Use when designing modules, seams, and adapters, when evaluating module depth and identifying deepening opportunities in a codebase, or when modernizing legacy code incrementally (strangler-fig, seams, characterization tests, safe extraction).

availableCommands.name: architecture-diagrams
availableCommands.description: Use when the deliverable is a physical diagram artifact (.svg/.png) — C4 models, dense class diagrams, network topology rendered via PlantUML. Not for diagrams embedded in Markdown (use Mermaid there).

availableCommands.name: arena
availableCommands.description: Use when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape. Spawns N parallel candidates at the same task, cross-judges, picks a base, grafts the strongest parts of the losers into it.

availableCommands.name: ascii-art
availableCommands.description: Use when generating animated ASCII art for artifacts the agent produces - README banners (SVG), CLI splash screens, loading/404 states or decorative pieces in web pages and terminals. Wraps the ascii.rest library (217 MIT pieces, React components, npx CLI, image-to-ascii).

availableCommands.name: ask-bundle
availableCommands.description: Use when deciding which skill or flow fits your situation — the meta-router entry point for this bundle (direct specialist skills, multi-skill flows, local AFK issues), or when the request is vague and needs the quick-start menu. Routes then defers to the chosen specialist — does not execute the work itself.

availableCommands.name: autonomous-gates
availableCommands.description: Use when running long-horizon or multi-step tasks where quality must be verified before proceeding, when the user asks for "autonomous mode" or "run unattended", or when a task has explicit acceptance criteria that must pass before declaring done.

availableCommands.name: benchmark-checklist
availableCommands.description: Use when running a benchmark, reporting a measured speedup or regression, or vetting a performance number before acting on it.

availableCommands.name: big-file-refactor
availableCommands.description: Use when a source file has grown past roughly 1000 lines, when context compaction is losing track of a file's content, or when asked to break an oversized file into modules safely.

availableCommands.name: binary-triage
availableCommands.description: Use when extracting evidence from closed binaries (DLL/SO/EXE/AAR) without heavy RE tooling - engine version, symbols, getter constants, exports, diff between builds, ctypes runtime probing. Answers in minutes what would take hours in Ghidra; escalate to re-binary/Ghidra only when static triage cannot close the question.

availableCommands.name: blast-radius
availableCommands.description: Use when asked for the blast radius of a change, what a diff could break elsewhere, or when reviewing a small diff you do not trust. Proves the one safety fact by running real code.

availableCommands.name: brag
availableCommands.description: Use when someone says /brag, let's brag about this, make a launch video, turn this into a video, or wants to share what they built. Turns the current project website into a short, polished, shareable launch video using Hyperframes, reading the project code directly with no live URL or screenshots needed.

availableCommands.name: brag-slim
availableCommands.description: Use when someone says /brag-slim, let's /brag about this, brag about a website, make a launch video, or wants to show off what they built. Turns a project directory or a website URL into a short, shareable launch video with music, motion, and share copy; one file, no bundled assets, built entirely by the model with the tools already on the machine. If the /brag skill is also installed, let /brag handle those phrases; it hands off here on Opus 5.5.

availableCommands.name: cli-adapter
availableCommands.description: Use when a tool or app has no MCP server or official connector, when the user asks the agent to control an application, or when a thin CLI wrapper is the cheapest integration path.

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Use when completing a task, reviewing a branch or PR, before merging, when the user asks to 'review since X', when publishing a GitHub PR review with inline comments/suggestions, or when the user receives code review feedback and needs to decide how to act on it.

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Use when designing modules, seams, adapters, and the structure of a codebase.

availableCommands.name: computer-use
availableCommands.description: Use when you need to see or control the local screen (screenshots, screen recording with video + contact sheet for catching transient bugs/animations, mouse clicks/movement, typing text and hotkeys) or to read/control terminals (Windows Terminal, conhost, mintty, spawned PTYs). GUI automation for desktop apps and browsers, replicating Devin Cloud Computer Use in the CLI.

availableCommands.name: context-folding
availableCommands.description: Use when context is growing large (approaching model window limits), when long documents or transcripts need to be processed, or when compaction is losing critical information. Adapts Recursive Language Model (RLM) techniques to the Devin CLI runtime.

availableCommands.name: context-hygiene
availableCommands.description: Use when context is growing large or the agent forgets earlier instructions, when deciding clear vs compact, when processing documents/logs >50k tokens, when monitoring token cost or limiting subagent fan-out, when choosing a reasoning effort level, or when reducing token/compute/MCP costs. Covers lost-in-the-middle, context folding (RLM), cost guards, and difficulty-matched effort.

availableCommands.name: context-window-hygiene
availableCommands.description: Use when a conversation is getting long and the agent seems to be forgetting earlier instructions, before adding MCP servers or rules files, when deciding whether to clear or compact the chat, or when context window budget feels tight. Covers lost-in-the-middle, clear-vs-compact, and lean-context hygiene.

availableCommands.name: context7
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks about a library, framework, or component and up-to-date docs would help.

availableCommands.name: continuous-improvement
availableCommands.description: Use when starting a self-improvement session. Enforces FASE 0 deep research and the 10-step improvement loop so no step is skipped, no phantom failure is invented, and every change is validated with held-out tests.

availableCommands.name: correct
availableCommands.description: Use when the operator corrects an agent mistake in the repo, or when hardening the project so a repeated agent mistake class cannot happen again.

availableCommands.name: cost-optimization
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to reduce token, compute, or infrastructure costs. Covers context window budget, MCP selection, caching, model routing, and query optimization.

availableCommands.name: create-verification-skill
availableCommands.description: Use when a project needs a scripted way to drive the real app the way a user does and prove behavior, or when asked to make a control/verification skill for the repo. Generates a project-local verify-<app> skill.

availableCommands.name: creative-engineering
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to apply a visual "style", "theme", or "effect" to code — frontend (CSS/GLSL), native shaders, or media processing (Python/OpenCV/FFmpeg) — especially CRT, dither, datamosh, night-vision, brutalist, receipt-print, depth-map, blob/metaball aesthetics. Loads a technical-anatomy knowledge base before writing code.

input.hint: Which visual style and target medium?

availableCommands.name: criador-de-devin-app
availableCommands.description: Use when turning a recurring intent into a named devin-cli app - a repeatable agent automation with its own name, schedule, prompt and done-when contract. Covers the agentic-app naming framework and the APP.md scaffold.

availableCommands.name: cu-realtime
availableCommands.description: Use when computer-use or terminal automation needs the fastest reaction the runtime allows - event waits instead of screenshot polling, text perception instead of image reads, whole perceive-act-verify cycles batched into one exec, or deterministic reflex loops below model latency. Composes with the `computer-use` skill (same extension CLIs).

availableCommands.name: data-analyst
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to query a database, analyze data, create charts/visualizations, explore data patterns, or asks business questions about data. Replicates Devin cloud's Data Analyst Agent (DANA) for the CLI — SQL-first exploration, schema-aware querying, and seaborn-style visualizations via MCP data sources.

availableCommands.name: database
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to design, migrate, query, or optimize a database. Covers schema design, migrations, query review, indexing, and data integrity.

availableCommands.name: de-slop
availableCommands.description: Use when cleaning a diff before opening a PR, or when asked to simplify, de-slop, or run the full quality pass on current changes.

availableCommands.name: debug-ci-failures
availableCommands.description: Use when CI is failing and the cause needs to be found across builds, jobs, or environments.

availableCommands.name: debugging
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says 'diagnose', 'debug this', reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow, when encountering a bug/test failure/unexpected behavior and a fix is not yet obvious, or when CI is failing and the cause needs to be found across builds, jobs, or environments.

availableCommands.name: deep-mode
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says 'deep', 'deep search', 'deep research', 'research this thoroughly', or asks for exhaustive codebase exploration beyond a quick grep. Replicates Ask Devin's Deep Mode (!deep in Slack/Teams) for the CLI - multi-pass agentic search with citations, cross-file synthesis, and architecture mapping.

availableCommands.name: deploy
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to release, deploy, rollback, or verify a deployment pipeline. Covers CI/CD gates, environment checks, canary/blue-green, and post-deploy smoke tests.

availableCommands.name: devin-config
availableCommands.description: Use when evolving the agent's capabilities with a new skill, custom subagent, plugin, hook, MCP server, or project rule — or when auditing/managing a project's `.devin/` configuration, producing deterministic read-only reports, detecting broken references/duplicates/divergences, and generating plans that persist under `.devin/` only after approval.

availableCommands.name: devin-manager
availableCommands.description: Use when auditing or managing a project's `.devin/` configuration, producing deterministic read-only reports, detecting broken references, duplicates, and divergences, and generating plans that only persist under `.devin/` after explicit approval.

availableCommands.name: diagnosing-bugs
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says 'diagnose', 'debug this', reports something broken, throwing, failing, or slow, or when encountering a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior and a fix is not yet obvious.

availableCommands.name: dispatching-parallel-agents
availableCommands.description: Use when facing two or more independent tasks with no shared state or ordering, OR when executing a multi-task plan by dispatching a fresh subagent per task.

availableCommands.name: dma
availableCommands.description: Use when the user invokes /dma or asks for a pentest, offensive recon, or aggressive audit on an authorized target. Dirty-work pentest agent and recon orchestrator - closes a scope contract with the user, classifies the target type, runs passive/static collection and surface mining, confirms vectors with minimal read-only probes inside the allowlist, and escalates deep testing via web-probe. Every invasive action requires explicit per-batch approval.

availableCommands.name: docker
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to build, run, compose, or deploy containers. Covers Dockerfiles, docker compose, images, volumes, networks, and basic Kubernetes manifests.

availableCommands.name: domain-modeling
availableCommands.description: Use when building or refining a project's domain model, glossary, or bounded contexts.

availableCommands.name: drift-report
availableCommands.description: Use when checking whether design documents, READMEs, or specs still match the code they describe. Reads each document, locates the referenced source files, and reports only concrete divergences in a dated drift report. Detection only; does not fix code or docs.

availableCommands.name: e2e-testing
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to add, run, or debug end-to-end tests. Covers Playwright, Selenium, Cypress, happy paths, critical user journeys, and CI integration. Browser-level journeys only; unit/TDD work goes to testing, test infrastructure to observability-quality.

availableCommands.name: edge-cases
availableCommands.description: Use when implementing a feature or bugfix, and before declaring done. Enumerate inputs/states/failure modes before coding, defend boundaries while coding, adversarially self-review the diff after. Prevents happy-path-only code.

availableCommands.name: edge-coverage
availableCommands.description: Use when assembling or auditing a test suite for rigorous edge-case coverage, when the user asks for meticulous test construction rules, boundary/equivalence analysis, or a completeness standard before a suite may be called done. Extends `testing`, `tdd`, `edge-cases`, and `mutation-testing` with a mandatory Edge Inventory that drives the suite.

availableCommands.name: effort-calibration
availableCommands.description: Use when choosing a reasoning effort level for an LLM coding agent, when a task seems to be over-thinking or spending too many tokens, when deciding whether to raise effort, when writing task specifications that substitute for reasoning budget, or when a simple task is being treated as a codebase audit. Covers overthinking, compute-optimal test-time scaling, prompt-induced waste, and difficulty-matched effort.

availableCommands.name: executing-plans
availableCommands.description: Use when executing a written implementation plan with checkpoints and reviews.

availableCommands.name: execution
availableCommands.description: Use when RUNNING an already-written plan/spec/tickets with checkpoints, implementing a feature/fix per spec, deciding how much human review a task needs, or working unattended through local Markdown issues in a blocking DAG (AFK loop). Plans get authored upstream in `planning`/`intake`.

availableCommands.name: fact-check
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to fact-check, tear apart, nitpick, or pre-publish-review an article, essay, blog post, or any markdown/text draft, verifying every checkable claim against online primary sources via adversarial checker subagents. Do not use for code review, security audits, or proofreading without factual verification.

availableCommands.name: finishing-a-development-branch
availableCommands.description: Use when the implementation is complete, all tests pass, and the work needs to be integrated.

availableCommands.name: forensic-debugging
availableCommands.description: Use when a bug, algorithm failure, or intermittent defect resists normal debugging, when an audit-grade trail of every hypothesis and experiment is required, or when the user asks for millimetric traceability to localize any failure fast. Extends `debugging` with a mandatory trace ledger, invariant map, and falsification protocol.

availableCommands.name: frontend-design
availableCommands.description: Use when building new UI or reshaping an existing one and the result must look distinctive and intentional, not templated. Guides aesthetic direction, typography, layout, and copy so the page has a specific point of view for this brief.

availableCommands.name: gates
availableCommands.description: Use when about to claim work is complete/fixed/passing, when a task risks agent laziness (large, multi-step, previously half-done, or with acceptance criteria), or when running long-horizon/unattended work where quality must be verified before proceeding. Covers gates, gates ledgers, and autonomous gate semantics. Completion-claim discipline only; writing tests goes to testing or e2e-testing.

availableCommands.name: gh
availableCommands.description: Use when interacting with GitHub via the gh CLI from an agent.

availableCommands.name: ghidra
availableCommands.description: Use when analyzing raw firmware images (ARM/Thumb embedded), dumped flash, or binaries without symbols - importing at a custom base address, seeding function discovery, and dumping decompiled output + xrefs for offline study via Ghidra headless.

availableCommands.name: git-helper
availableCommands.description: Use when managing branches, writing commits, or resolving simple git workflow questions.

availableCommands.name: git-workflows
availableCommands.description: Use when managing branches, writing commits, creating isolated worktrees for feature work, or resolving and verifying merge/rebase conflicts.

availableCommands.name: github-actions
availableCommands.description: Use when writing or reviewing .github/workflows YAML files or debugging CI. GitHub Actions security and best practices - SHA-pinned actions, least-privilege permissions, script injection via PR context, pull_request_target dangers, secrets and OIDC, cache poisoning, matrix and artifacts.

availableCommands.name: grilling
availableCommands.description: Use when exploring and stress-testing ideas before committing to a design or plan, when the user says "grill me" or "stress-test this", or when sharpening a plan while also producing ADRs and a glossary.

availableCommands.name: handoff
availableCommands.description: Use when the user needs to compact the current conversation into a document for another agent to continue.

input.hint: What will the next session be used for?

availableCommands.name: humanizer
availableCommands.description: Use when editing or reviewing prose for AI tells and rewriting it so it reads like the writer without changing what it says. Covers not-X-but-Y contrasts, one-line closers, staged openers, forced triads, dashes used everywhere, inflated claims, sales language, stock AI words, bold labels, and filler. Do not use for code, data, or factual verification.

availableCommands.name: hyperframes
availableCommands.description: Use when turning HTML/data-attribute animations into MP4 video (kinetic text, web-native motion graphics, DOM-driven scenes). Routes to extensions/hyperframes/wrapper.py, a whitelist passthrough to the hyperframes CLI over npx (Node >= 22 + FFmpeg required).

availableCommands.name: i18n
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to add or review internationalization and localization. Covers locale files, translation keys, pluralization, RTL, and date/number formatting.

availableCommands.name: image-forensics
availableCommands.description: Use when checking whether an image is a real camera capture or synthetic/generated, when tagging media provenance before ingestion, when verifying visual evidence for fact-check, or when validating that ai3d-gen source photos are real captures before splatting. Covers PRNU noise-residual forensics, EXIF/XMP/C2PA first pass, and PCE scoring via extensions/image-forensics.

availableCommands.name: impeccable
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for UI/UX work, wants to fix or polish a page/component, or when an interface looks bland, inconsistent, or like a default template.

availableCommands.name: implement
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to implement a feature or fix from a spec or set of tickets.

availableCommands.name: implement-laya
availableCommands.description: Use when a task needs fast typed decisions — classification, triage, scoring, guardrails, moderation, or model routing — over text/JSON states, or when integrating the `laya` engine (non-autoregressive decision model) into a user's codebase.

input.hint: What decision should the engine make?

availableCommands.name: improve-codebase-architecture
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to evaluate module depth, identify deepening opportunities in a codebase, and act on them.

availableCommands.name: intake
availableCommands.description: Use when SIZING a task or PR and deciding whether to split it, validating the "intent" field in tickets/specs/PRDs before implementation, or moving issues and external PRs through triage states (categorise, verify, grill, write agent-ready briefs). Feeds `planning`; does not author plans.

availableCommands.name: intention-capture
availableCommands.description: Use when capturing and validating the "intent" field in tickets, specs, or PRDs before implementation. Ensures every task has a clear objective, landing zone, and user impact.

availableCommands.name: jira
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to interact with Jira — search issues, read or update tickets, transition status, add comments, list projects, or run JQL. Routes operations through the Atlassian Rovo MCP server (mcp__atlassian__* tools).

availableCommands.name: knowledge-modeling
availableCommands.description: Use when building or refining a project's domain model, glossary, or bounded contexts, when validating tool outputs/data against a domain ontology before side effects, or when extracting entities, relations, evidence, and provenance from Markdown/plain text into a typed versioned knowledge graph under `.devin/`.

availableCommands.name: laya-orchestrator
availableCommands.description: Use when a cheap typed check beats reading files into context - batch file classification (contains auth data? has tests?), review risk scoring, or pre-dispatch triage. Laya ranks and abstains, never proves - it is not a substitute for reading primary sources (Rule 12).

availableCommands.name: lean-code
availableCommands.description: Use when writing, fixing, refactoring, or reviewing code, choosing dependencies, or when the user asks for the simplest solution, minimal diff, yagni, or complains about over-engineering or bloat.

availableCommands.name: legacy-refactor
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to modernize legacy code incrementally. Covers strangler-fig, seams, characterization tests, safe extraction, and risk reduction.

availableCommands.name: leo
availableCommands.description: Use when routing and orchestrating any work across this Devin bundle through one universal entry point, including direct specialist skills, multi-skill flows, and local AFK issues.

availableCommands.name: lgpd-questionnaire
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks for an LGPD/data-protection compliance review of an app or service - data inventory, legal basis, third-party sharing, subject rights, breach response. Produces an evidence-cited compliance matrix, not legal advice.

availableCommands.name: maintain-verification-skill
availableCommands.description: Use when keeping a project's verification skill and feature map honest as the app changes. Source-reader fan-out per feature plus one live driving pass; ships at most one PR of proven corrections.

availableCommands.name: mcp-context-audit
availableCommands.description: Use when considering adding an MCP server, when context feels bloated with tool definitions, when auditing which MCP servers consume the most context window budget, or before committing a change to mcp_config.json. Estimates per-server tool-definition token cost and flags bloat.

availableCommands.name: mcp-governance
availableCommands.description: Use when considering adding an MCP server, when context feels bloated with tool definitions, when auditing which servers consume the most context budget, before committing mcp_config.json changes, or when deciding which servers to keep active per task. Estimates per-server tool-definition token cost and guides lazy enablement.

availableCommands.name: mcp-lazy-enablement
availableCommands.description: Use when deciding which MCP servers to keep active, when context feels bloated from unused MCP tools, when a task only needs one MCP server temporarily, or when auditing which servers to enable/disable per task. Guides selective MCP enablement to minimize context-window tax.

availableCommands.name: media-tools
availableCommands.description: Use when generating visual artifacts — ASCII art, halftone, dithering, matrix-rain, VHS, pixel-sort, voronoi, and other image/video FX — from images, GIFs, videos, GLB models, or webcam input. Local, offline-first.

input.hint: What visual artifact should I generate?

availableCommands.name: memory-hygiene
availableCommands.description: Use when deciding whether to use cross-session agent memory (MEMORY.md, auto-memory), when auto-memory seems stale or bloated, when preferences leak across unrelated tasks, or when choosing between stateless and memory-equipped operation. Covers memory accumulation, temporal contamination, reasoning drift, and user-authored vs auto-saved preferences.

availableCommands.name: mesh-utils
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to inspect, convert, clean, or validate mesh/3D scene files (OBJ, STL, GLB, FBX, USD) via trimesh, PyMeshLab, or pxr. Routes to extensions/mesh-utils/meshops.py. Lightweight stdlib CLI; deps are pip-installed only when needed.

availableCommands.name: mutation-testing
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to find testing gaps, mutation test, or identify surviving mutants.

availableCommands.name: no-comments
availableCommands.description: Use when hunting comment smells, workaround comments, or stale suppressions on a diff, or when asked to delete comments and encode claimed constraints before a PR.

availableCommands.name: observability-quality
availableCommands.description: Use when adding logging, metrics, distributed tracing, error monitoring, linting, architecture testing, or test infrastructure to a project. Covers OpenTelemetry, Sentry/Datadog/Grafana, Biome/ESLint, ArchUnit, commitlint, Knip, Playwright, and coverage strategy. Infrastructure and tooling quality only; writing feature tests goes to testing or e2e-testing.

availableCommands.name: obsidian-workflow
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to build or update a local codebase wiki in Obsidian with architecture diagrams, source-linked documentation, hierarchical pages, auto-refresh, effort levels (low/medium/high), Deep Research pass (architecture critique, anti-patterns, tech debt), and conversational Q&A via deep-mode; or reorganize, refactor, or restructure an Obsidian vault, knowledge base, or documentation folder; or audit, validate, or fix Obsidian project wikis (broken wikilinks, source citations, diagrams, sensitive info, language); or compare wiki knowledge by source session or source type to surface cross-session blind spots.

availableCommands.name: ontology-validator
availableCommands.description: Use when validating tool outputs or data against a domain ontology or structured knowledge base. Ensures entities, types, and relations are consistent before side effects.

availableCommands.name: operate-blender
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to create, build, manipulate, render, animate, or export 3D content (scenes, models, characters, environments, stylized/cartoon or hyper-real art, procedural geometry). Routes to extensions/blender-operator/wrapper.py, which drives headless Blender through a TCP exec loop with full bpy access; no GUI, no MCP addon, free/GPL tooling.

availableCommands.name: operate-godot
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to build, inspect, import assets into, or export a Godot 4 project headlessly (realtime 3D delivery, game scenes, interactive world execution). Uses godot --headless --script CLI; no GUI. Free/MIT engine.

availableCommands.name: operate-spline
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to launch, drive, build scenes in, export from, or shut down the Spline desktop app (3D/2D design, Electron). Routes to extensions/spline-operator/wrapper.py, which speaks the app's embedded MCP bridge (ws://127.0.0.1:19692) - structured tool calls, not GUI clicking.

availableCommands.name: performance
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to profile, optimize, load-test, or measure the performance of code, queries, or infrastructure.

availableCommands.name: planning
availableCommands.description: Use when AUTHORING a spec/PRD, implementation plan, or ticket breakdown from conversation — writing the artifacts, not running them. Hands off to `execution` once the plan exists. Also for decisions needing external input via questionnaire, or work too large for one session mapped as decision tickets (wayfinding).

availableCommands.name: planning-pipeline
availableCommands.description: Use when turning conversation into a written spec, breaking a plan or spec into independent traceable tickets, or when a decision cannot be fully answered and needs input from another person via a questionnaire.

availableCommands.name: playbook
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to create, refine, or use a reusable playbook for repeated tasks — a structured prompt template with Procedure, Specifications, Advice, Forbidden Actions, and Required-from-User sections. Replicates Devin cloud's Playbook feature (.devin.md files, macros, team/community library) for the CLI.

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Use when writing a PR body or description — a visual Summary (smallest diagram/diff-sketch/tree that makes the point), concrete Evidence (before/after runs), and Merge Danger (one-way vs two-way door + blast radius). Ported and adapted from mattpocock/skills engineering/pr.

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to review a Pull Request on GitHub with inline comments and code suggestions via the GitHub API. Enforces a repeatable cycle of check -> comment/suggest -> check next, with a gates ledger for evidence.

availableCommands.name: primeagent-reference
availableCommands.description: Use when (1) researching agent harness design patterns, comparing Devin CLI to PrimeAgent/RLM architectures, or evaluating which PrimeAgent features could be adapted to Devin CLI; (2) emulating A2A messaging between subagents or between subagents and the parent agent across time within Devin CLI's ephemeral subagent runtime; (3) capturing recurring failure patterns or reusable tactics as skills/rules/hooks via the Continual Harness /refine self-improvement loop; or (4) deciding whether to dispatch a subagent, which profile to use, and how many concurrent agents to run (subagent dispatch profile/budget selection).

availableCommands.name: project-bootstrap
availableCommands.description: Use when starting work on a project that lacks a `.devin/` configuration, when the user wants to add skills/hooks/rules/local tools systematically, when configuring a repo's issue tracker + triage labels + domain docs for the engineering skills, or when setting up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged/typecheck/tests.

availableCommands.name: project-memory
availableCommands.description: Use when the session produces knowledge worth remembering across sessions, such as answered user questions, business rules, project conventions, failed approaches, reusable solutions, or decisions. Captures it with user approval and stores it as plain-text notes inside .devin/ for future retrieval.

availableCommands.name: project-orchestrator
availableCommands.description: Use when driving a project from an empty folder or a fuzzy idea to a delivered product with CI/CD, coordinating specialist subagents under delegation contracts, producing the methodology documentation that fits the scope (RUP / Scrum / hybrid), with verified research before technology decisions and an excellence gate that reviews screen recordings of the real user path.

availableCommands.name: project-setup
availableCommands.description: Use when starting work on a new or existing project that lacks a `.devin/` configuration, or when the user wants to add skills, hooks, rules, and local tools to a project in a systematic, validated way.

availableCommands.name: prompt-compiler
availableCommands.description: Use when the user invokes /prompt or asks to compile, refine, or optimize a prompt before execution — interactive pre-flight optimizer that produces an approved super-prompt saved to .devin/scratch/optimized_ready.md.

input.hint: What task should the compiled prompt execute?

availableCommands.name: prototype
availableCommands.description: Use when a throwaway prototype is the fastest way to answer a design question.

availableCommands.name: rag
availableCommands.description: Use when building retrieval over a project corpus (docs, code, notes), when answering chunking/embedding/vector-store questions, when evaluating whether retrieval actually works, or when an agent "can't find things in the docs" and grep alone is not cutting it.

availableCommands.name: re-binary
availableCommands.description: Use when reverse-engineering a declared binary, library, APK, firmware image, or script artifact under an engagement contract (native code, .NET, Java/Android, Electron/JS, browser extensions). Routes to extensions/rea-ops/wrapper.py, a whitelist passthrough to the rea-agents CLI (Hopper/Ghidra engines probed via doctor).

availableCommands.name: receiving-code-review
availableCommands.description: Use when the user receives code review feedback and needs to decide how to act on it.

availableCommands.name: red-team
availableCommands.description: Use when running an authorized offensive-security engagement against a declared target (binary, web app, network, wireless, firmware, mobile). Routes to domain skills (re-binary, web-probe, net-probe, wireless-probe, firmware-probe, mobile-probe) and enforces the engagement contract (target/window/ROE) plus evidence discipline.

availableCommands.name: research
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks a question that needs investigation against primary sources and citations, or says 'deep', 'deep search', 'deep research', 'research this thoroughly', or asks for exhaustive codebase exploration beyond a quick grep. Covers external primary-source research (background agent) and multi-pass deep codebase search with citations.

availableCommands.name: resolving-merge-conflicts
availableCommands.description: Use when a merge conflict needs to be resolved and verified.

availableCommands.name: retro
availableCommands.description: Use when conducting a retrospective on a coding session to improve the agent's environment for future runs — navigation pointers, automated guardrails, reviewer standards, rules-file hygiene, tool economy, information access. Lightweight per-session review; deeper self-improvement loops go to continuous-improvement.

availableCommands.name: review-cadence
availableCommands.description: Use when deciding how much human review and upfront planning a task needs based on its size, risk, and blast radius, or when the user asks whether a change can skip grilling and go straight to implementation.

availableCommands.name: scheduled-turns
availableCommands.description: Use when a task needs recurring or always-on agent turns (periodic checks, polling workflows, run-this-every-morning jobs) without adding a daemon. OS scheduler plus one-shot headless Devin turns writing to ledgers.

availableCommands.name: scrape-tools
availableCommands.description: Use when a task needs structured data extracted from web pages or HTML files - CSS/XPath selection, TLS-impersonated fetching, adaptive selectors that survive markup churn. Routes to extensions/scrape-tools.

availableCommands.name: secure-defaults-check
availableCommands.description: Use when checking that a project or change follows secure defaults before committing or deploying.

availableCommands.name: security
availableCommands.description: Use when auditing code, dependencies, or infrastructure for security issues (SAST, dependency scanning, secret leak detection, OWASP-style checks), or when checking that a project or change follows secure defaults before committing or deploying.

availableCommands.name: security-audit
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to audit code, dependencies, or infrastructure for security issues. Covers SAST, dependency scanning, secret leak detection, and OWASP-style checks.

availableCommands.name: security-audit-cf
availableCommands.description: Use when security guidance and vulnerability review is needed for codebases, APIs, services, CLI tools, libraries, and daemons. Use for security questions, focused reviews, vulnerability research, security audits, or pen tests. Run the complete workflow only for explicit codebase audit or pen-test requests, full/comprehensive/end-to-end reviews, or requested report artifacts.

availableCommands.name: self-extend
availableCommands.description: Use when evolving the agent's own capabilities with a new skill, custom subagent, plugin, hook, MCP server, or project rule.

availableCommands.name: setup-engineering-skills
availableCommands.description: Use when configuring a repo for the engineering skills - set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, and domain doc layout. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.

availableCommands.name: setup-pre-commit
availableCommands.description: Use when setting up Husky pre-commit hooks with lint-staged (Prettier), type checking, and tests in the current repo. Covers adding pre-commit hooks, configuring Husky, lint-staged, or commit-time formatting/typechecking/testing.

availableCommands.name: shorts-factory
availableCommands.description: Use when producing short-form vertical or square videos (Shorts, Reels, TikTok) end to end from a topic -- script, narration, alignment, stock b-roll, scene plan, render, and ffmpeg composite with captions. Assembles tts + extensions/asr + extensions/stock-footage + animation-direction/remotion-render into a MoneyPrinterTurbo-equivalent pipeline.

availableCommands.name: skill-discovery
availableCommands.description: Use when starting any non-trivial task, before taking any action a skill might apply to, when the user asks how to do something, when no skill seems to match, or when discovering, installing, or evaluating a new skill for Devin CLI.

availableCommands.name: social-midia
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to draft, post, schedule, or analyze content on a social network (LinkedIn, X/Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Reddit), asks about a platform's official API (auth, scopes, endpoints, rate limits, analytics), or needs cross-network publishing workflows. Routes to the per-network skill; does not execute the work itself.

availableCommands.name: structured-knowledge-extraction
availableCommands.description: Use when extracting entities, relations, evidence, and provenance from Markdown or plain text into a typed, versioned knowledge graph under `.devin/`.

availableCommands.name: system-control
availableCommands.description: Use when the task needs authorized OS-level control — process inventory, service status, bounded one-shot command execution, persistent owned sessions, event streams, or root-bound verified file copies — where native system APIs beat GUI computer-use. Routes to the system-control extension.

availableCommands.name: task-sizer
availableCommands.description: Use when estimating the size of a task or PR and deciding whether to split it into smaller tickets before implementation.

availableCommands.name: tdd
availableCommands.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix and a test-driven approach is appropriate.

availableCommands.name: teach
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to learn a skill or concept through a guided, multi-step session.

input.hint: What would you like to learn about?

availableCommands.name: testing
availableCommands.description: Use when implementing any feature or bugfix and a test-driven approach is appropriate (red-green-refactor, seams-first), or when the user asks to find testing gaps, mutation test, or identify surviving mutants. Unit and integration tests only; browser journeys go to e2e-testing, test infrastructure to observability-quality, completion claims to gates.

availableCommands.name: thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review
availableCommands.description: Use when running an extremely strict maintainability review for abstraction quality, giant files, and spaghetti-condition growth, for a thermo-nuclear code quality review, thermonuclear review, deep code quality audit, or especially harsh maintainability review.

availableCommands.name: thermo-nuclear-review
availableCommands.description: Use when a comprehensive security and correctness audit of a branch's changes is needed, for thermo nuclear, thermonuclear, or deep review requests, or branch/PR diff audits focused on bugs, breaking changes, security issues, devex regressions, and feature-gate leaks.

availableCommands.name: thermos
availableCommands.description: Use when launching both thermo-nuclear review subagents in parallel and synthesizing their findings, for thermos, double thermo review, or combined bug/security and code-quality branch audits.

availableCommands.name: tool-and-skill-discovery
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks how to do something, needs the right skill or tool, no skill seems to match the task, or wants to discover, install, or evaluate a new skill for Devin CLI.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: Use when moving issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles - categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

availableCommands.name: tts
availableCommands.description: Use when generating speech, narration, voiceover, or any text-to-speech audio locally. Routes to extensions/voicebox/wrapper.py, an HTTP client for a user-started voicebox backend (jamiepine/voicebox, FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:17493).

availableCommands.name: typescript-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Use when reading or editing any .ts or .tsx file for TypeScript best practices.

availableCommands.name: typescript-node
availableCommands.description: Use when writing or reviewing TypeScript or Node.js code. Strict mode, async/await footguns, error handling, null safety, real types vs any, ESM/CJS interop, npm hygiene (engines, lockfile, scripts, ci).

availableCommands.name: unlazy
availableCommands.description: Use when a task is at risk of agent laziness (large, multi-step, previously half-done, or with clear acceptance criteria) to force proof of completion through a gates ledger instead of trusting agent reports.

availableCommands.name: unslop
availableCommands.description: Use when editing or reviewing prose to remove AI writing patterns. Cuts AI tells from any writing.

availableCommands.name: using-git-worktrees
availableCommands.description: Use when starting feature work that needs isolation from the current workspace.

availableCommands.name: using-skills
availableCommands.description: Use when starting any conversation and before taking any non-trivial action.

availableCommands.name: vercel-react-best-practices
availableCommands.description: Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code for optimal performance. React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering; triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.

availableCommands.name: verification-before-completion
availableCommands.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing.

availableCommands.name: wait-what
availableCommands.description: Use when the last message did not land and needs to be re-explained or re-pitched.

availableCommands.name: wayfinder
availableCommands.description: Use when planning work too large for one session as a map of decision tickets.

availableCommands.name: web-perf-checklist
availableCommands.description: Use when a web app feels slow, when a PR touches frontend/backend performance, or when asked for the concrete fix-list behind a performance complaint.

availableCommands.name: webhooks
availableCommands.description: Use when building or debugging endpoints that receive third-party callbacks (payments, GitHub, ERP). Webhook receiver discipline - signature verification, idempotency by event id, fast acknowledge with background processing, replay protection.

availableCommands.name: wizard
availableCommands.description: Use when a human must walk through a manual procedure such as provisioning, credentials, or a one-off cutover.

availableCommands.name: writing-for-agents
availableCommands.description: Use when creating or editing skills, `.devin/global_rules.md` / `.devin/rules/*.md` rules, or other docs an agent must read.

availableCommands.name: writing-plans
availableCommands.description: Use when turning a spec into a concrete, task-by-task implementation plan.

availableCommands.name: writing-skills
availableCommands.description: Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, verifying skills work before deployment, or when creating/editing any document an agent must read (`.devin/global_rules.md`, `.devin/rules/*.md`, docs reached by pointer).

availableCommands.name: youtube-fetcher
availableCommands.description: Use when you need to turn a YouTube URL and provider-supplied caption/metadata JSON into a raw, timestamped transcript + metadata Markdown note under `.devin/notes/youtube/` for later structured extraction, without auto-installing dependencies, invoking yt-dlp/Whisper, or calling the network. Not for publishing or posting to YouTube; use social-midia/youtube for that.

availableCommands.name: rts-3d-procedural-art
availableCommands.description: Use when building or upgrading 2D/isometric/top-down games or canvases to look like pre-rendered 3D (Warcraft III, Age of Empires III, Hades) with PBR-style lighting, directional cast shadows, seamless terrain splatting, Gerstner water waves, skeletal IK/FK locomotion, and Verlet cloth physics without external 3D asset files.

availableCommands.name: rts-hud-audio-design
availableCommands.description: Use when designing or overhauling RTS user interfaces, command cards, hotkey grids, tooltips, game menus, or procedural WebAudio sound effects (Karplus-Strong strings, FM metallic clashes, filtered noise wind/rain/thunder, and theme-specific foley).

availableCommands.name: verify-atlas
availableCommands.description: Use when changing the GitHub Pages atlas (site/src/*, site/build.py, data inputs like manifest/CHANGELOG) and a real end-to-end proof is needed that the built site actually works - boot, tabs, skill cards, REPL, palette. Project-local verification skill generated via create-verification-skill.

availableCommands.name: declarative-repo-setup
availableCommands.description: Generate and verify a working environment.yaml (Devin snapshot-setup blueprint) for a repo

availableCommands.name: upload-secrets
availableCommands.description: Securely upload local secrets (dotenv files, env vars, API keys) to the Devin Cloud secrets manager — values never enter the conversation
